title: Verified teaching additions · Newtonian motion
source_policy: Curated teaching additions, checked against the linked primary educational publishers on 2026-10-07. Original uploaded graph records remain unchanged. Arrows follow the predicate, not a claim that every connection is causal.

source_claims.statement: For a constant positive mass in a Newtonian inertial frame, net external force determines acceleration by the vector relation a = F_net / m; at fixed net force, acceleration is inversely proportional to mass.

references.title: OpenStax University Physics Volume 1, §5.3 Newton’s Second Law
references.section: Newton’s Second Law of Motion; equation 5.3

edges.mechanism: Net external force produces acceleration in the same direction.
edges.conditions: Newtonian mechanics; inertial reference frame; constant positive mass; vector net external force (not an individual unbalanced component assumed in isolation).

edges.mechanism: At fixed net external force, a larger mass gives a smaller acceleration; this is a conditional dependence, not mass alone causing motion.
edges.conditions: Newtonian inertial frame; compare constant positive masses under the same net external force.
